title: Instrumenting your own service: the OpenTelemetry SDK, spans and attributes

videos.script: In lesson 1, the slow checkout was found by a span called wait for the card network. Somebody wrote that span. {{span}} This lesson is about writing them. You start with a script that creates a span and nothing happens. No error, no output, nothing recorded. {{nothing}} That silence is deliberate, and it explains how OpenTelemetry is built. There is an API, which your code calls. And there is an SDK, which decides whether anything is recorded and where it goes. {{split}} You add the SDK, and the span prints. You nest spans and watch the parent ids line up. You read the storefront's own code, and see which attributes it records and which it refuses to. {{code}} Then you break the shop on purpose, and find the error in the trace. You measure what exporting costs. And you see why a span's name must never contain an order number. {{names}}
